confidence_notes: Food and drink anchors come from three web searches: the RBA rate, a Lucerne cost-of-living and price search, and a Lucerne cocktail and wine menu search. Sources gave a cappuccino at about CHF 5, a 0.5 L beer at about CHF 7-9, and an inexpensive meal at about CHF 25-45. A 3-course meal for two and the cocktail and wine anchors are less certain. The cocktail and wine figures rest on a few hotel-bar menus (cocktail around CHF 23 at a luxury hotel, 10 cl wine at CHF 10-12). I scaled those down to typical venues and set them relative to beer. I converted CHF to USD at an assumed rate of about 1.25 USD per CHF. Accommodation anchors are holistic model estimates for July peak season. I did not search for or inspect any accommodation prices. Swiss hostel and hotel rates vary widely, so those are the least certain.
comparable_city_reasoning: Lucerne is a high-priced Swiss tourist city. I treated it as roughly in line with Zurich and Geneva for food and drink, slightly cheaper, and with strong summer accommodation demand.
